# instruction.md

## UK Retail Fuel Price Trend Analysis — February 2026

You are tasked with producing a professional data analysis report examining retail fuel pricing patterns across UK forecourts. This report will be read by **government policy analysts and energy economists** who need evidence-based insights into market competitiveness, pricing transparency, and retailer reporting behaviour. It should directly inform decisions around consumer protection policy and fuel market regulation.

### Context & Purpose

The UK government mandates open reporting of forecourt fuel prices. Your job is to analyse this dataset and surface meaningful patterns: How do prices vary across fuel types? Are consumers in some areas paying significantly more than others? How promptly are retailers updating their reported prices? These questions matter for assessing whether the market is functioning transparently and competitively.

### Key Priorities

- **Price distribution by fuel type is the centrepiece** of this report. Ensure the statistics (mean, median, spread) are clearly presented with supporting visualisations — box plots or violin plots work well here.
- **Price spread and competitiveness analysis** is the most policy-relevant section. Emphasise the IQR and max-min range to show whether consumers face meaningful price disparities.
- **Update freshness analysis** is critical for assessing data quality and retailer compliance. Calculate the lag between `source_updated_at` and `recorded_at` carefully and flag any concerning patterns.
- The **Key Findings** section must be executive-friendly — concise, numbered, and tied to policy implications.

### Data Integrity

**Absolutely no fabrication.** Every number, statistic, and claim in the report must be derived directly from `data.csv`. If data is missing or incomplete, note it transparently rather than filling gaps with assumptions.

### Output

Deliver the final report as **`/app/output/final_report.html`**. Use a clean, professional layout with an analytical tone. Embed all charts inline.

Refer to `task_input.json` for the full specification of required sections, KPIs, and analysis dimensions.

---

## Data Sources

1. Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md` for dataset documentation and column descriptions.
2. Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json` for report requirements, KPIs, and analysis dimensions.
3. Read `/app/benchmark/data.csv` as the primary dataset to analyze.

## Output Requirements

1. Output the final report to `/app/output/`. Use the filename and format specified in the instruction above.
2. All visualizations must be embedded in the report (inline SVG, base64 images, or chart libraries loaded via CDN).
3. The report must be self-contained — openable directly in a browser (if HTML) or readable as-is (if PDF).

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or wait-for-user instructions, make a professional judgment and continue.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies `report.tone`, `report.audience`, etc., use them to choose color schemes, chart types, and layout styles. Otherwise, make professional judgments.
3. **Priority** — these rules override any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The skill's workflow, quality standards, and technical specs remain fully effective — only skip interactive waits.

# UK Retail Fuel Prices — Price History Dataset

## About the Dataset

This dataset is sourced from **Kaggle (jamesb7/fuel-prices-uk)** and provides UK retail fuel prices at an individual forecourt level, originally collected from the UK Government's official Fuel Finder API. The data is aggregated by [fuelcosts.co.uk](https://fuelcosts.co.uk), a fuel price comparison platform covering over 8,000 petrol stations across England, Scotland, and Wales.

The file `price_history.csv` contains **396,502 rows** and **6 columns**. Each row represents a single fuel price observation at a specific station at a specific point in time.

## Column Schema

| Column Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | Integer | Unique auto-incrementing identifier for each price record. |
| `node_id` | String | Hashed identifier for the fuel station (forecourt). Each unique value represents a distinct station. These are SHA-style hashes (64+ characters), not human-readable names. |
| `fuel_type` | String | The type of fuel. Known values include: **E10** (standard unleaded petrol), **B7_STANDARD** (standard diesel), **E5** (super unleaded petrol), and potentially premium diesel variants. |
| `price_pence` | Integer | The retail price of the fuel in **pence per litre (PPL)**. Whole number values (e.g., 133 means £1.33/litre). |
| `recorded_at` | String (ISO 8601 datetime) | Timestamp when the price was recorded/collected into the dataset. Format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`. |
| `source_updated_at` | String (ISO 8601 datetime) | Timestamp when the retailer last updated/reported this price to the government feed. Format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`. |

## Key Column Details

### fuel_type
The dataset covers multiple fuel types mandated under the UK open data scheme:
- **E10**: Standard unleaded petrol (the default grade at most UK pumps since 2021)
- **B7_STANDARD**: Standard diesel (containing up to 7% biodiesel)
- **E5**: Super unleaded petrol (higher octane, contains up to 5% ethanol)
- Other premium or specialty fuels may also appear

Not all stations sell every fuel type — some may only report E10 and B7_STANDARD.

### node_id
Station identifiers are anonymised hashes. Without a separate station metadata lookup table, individual station names, brands, or geographic locations cannot be determined from this file alone. However, the `node_id` can be used to group records by station and analyse per-station behaviour.

### Timestamps
The difference between `recorded_at` and `source_updated_at` is analytically meaningful. `source_updated_at` reflects when the retailer actually changed or confirmed their price, while `recorded_at` reflects when the data collection system captured it. The lag between these two timestamps can indicate how fresh the data is and how frequently retailers update their feeds.

## Data Quality Notes

- **No missing values** are apparent in the sample, but analysts should verify for nulls across the full 396,502 rows.
- **Price values** are integers in pence. Typical UK fuel prices in early 2026 range roughly from 125 to 165+ pence per litre depending on fuel type and location. Outliers outside this range should be investigated.
- **Timestamps** are in UTC (indicated by the `Z` suffix). All datetime parsing should account for ISO 8601 format.
- The sample data is from **early February 2026**. The full dataset's date range should be confirmed during analysis.
- Since station metadata (brand, address, coordinates) is not included in this CSV, geographic or brand-level analysis is not possible with this file alone.

## Attribution

- Data compiled by fuelcosts.co.uk
- Source data: UK Government Fuel Finder scheme
- License: CC BY 4.0

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
UK Retail Fuel Price Trend Analysis — February 2026
Report generation script: analyses data.csv and produces final_report.html
"""

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import base64
from io import BytesIO
from datetime import datetime
from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, BaseLoader
import json
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# ── Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DATA_PATH = '/app/benchmark/data.csv'
OUTPUT_DIR = '/app/output/'
REPORT_PATH = OUTPUT_DIR + 'final_report.html'

# Colour palette – professional, analytical tone
PALETTE = {
    'E10': '#2563EB',
    'B7_STANDARD': '#DC2626',
    'E5': '#059669',
    'B7_PREMIUM': '#7C3AED',
    'B10': '#D97706',
    'SDV': '#DB2777',
}
NEUTRAL = '#6B7280'
LIGHT_BG = '#F9FAFB'
GRID_CLR = '#E5E7EB'

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'sans-serif',
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.titlesize': 13,
    'axes.labelsize': 11,
    'figure.facecolor': 'white',
    'axes.facecolor': LIGHT_BG,
    'axes.grid': True,
    'grid.color': GRID_CLR,
    'grid.linewidth': 0.6,
})

# ── Helper: matplotlib figure → base64 ────────────────────────────────────
def fig_to_b64(fig, dpi=150):
    buf = BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=dpi, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
    buf.seek(0)
    b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.read()).decode('utf-8')
    plt.close(fig)
    return b64

# ── Load Data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("Loading data...")
df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH, parse_dates=['recorded_at', 'source_updated_at'])
print(f"  Records loaded: {len(df):,}")

# ── Section 1: Dataset Overview ───────────────────────────────────────────
total_records = len(df)
unique_stations = df['node_id'].nunique()
fuel_types = sorted(df['fuel_type'].unique())
date_range_start = df['recorded_at'].min()
date_range_end = df['recorded_at'].max()
date_range_str = f"{date_range_start.strftime('%d %B %Y')} – {date_range_end.strftime('%d %B %Y')}"
null_counts = df.isnull().sum().to_dict()

fuel_type_counts = df.groupby('fuel_type').size().sort_values(ascending=False).to_dict()

print(f"  Unique stations: {unique_stations:,}")
print(f"  Fuel types: {fuel_types}")
print(f"  Date range: {date_range_str}")

# ── Section 2: Price Distribution by Fuel Type ────────────────────────────
print("\nAnalysing price distributions...")
price_stats = df.groupby('fuel_type')['price_pence'].agg(
    count='count',
    mean='mean',
    median='median',
    std='std',
    min='min',
    max='max',
    q25=lambda x: x.quantile(0.25),
    q75=lambda x: x.quantile(0.75),
).sort_values('count', ascending=False)
price_stats['iqr'] = price_stats['q75'] - price_stats['q25']
price_stats['spread'] = price_stats['max'] - price_stats['min']

# Round for display
price_stats_display = price_stats.copy()
for col in ['mean', 'median', 'std', 'min', 'max', 'q25', 'q75', 'iqr', 'spread']:
    price_stats_display[col] = price_stats_display[col].round(1)

print(price_stats_display[['count', 'mean', 'median', 'std', 'min', 'max', 'iqr', 'spread']])

# ── Chart 2a: Box plot of price by fuel type ──────────────────────────────
fuel_order = price_stats.index.tolist()
fig_box, ax_box = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
box_data = [df.loc[df['fuel_type'] == ft, 'price_pence'].values for ft in fuel_order]
bp = ax_box.boxplot(box_data, labels=fuel_order, patch_artist=True, showfliers=True,
                    flierprops=dict(marker='o', markersize=2, alpha=0.3),
                    whiskerprops=dict(linewidth=1.2),
                    medianprops=dict(linewidth=2, color='#1F2937'),
                    capprops=dict(linewidth=1.2))
for patch, ft in zip(bp['boxes'], fuel_order):
    patch.set_facecolor(PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL))
    patch.set_alpha(0.7)
ax_box.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)')
ax_box.set_xlabel('Fuel Type')
ax_box.set_title('Price Distribution by Fuel Type')
ax_box.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FormatStrFormatter('%d'))
fig_box.tight_layout()
chart_box_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_box)

# ── Chart 2b: Violin plot ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig_violin, ax_violin = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
parts = ax_violin.violinplot(box_data, positions=range(1, len(fuel_order)+1),
                              showmeans=True, showmedians=True, showextrema=False)
for i, pc in enumerate(parts['bodies']):
    pc.set_facecolor(PALETTE.get(fuel_order[i], NEUTRAL))
    pc.set_alpha(0.6)
parts['cmeans'].set_color('#1F2937')
parts['cmeans'].set_linewidth(1.5)
parts['cmedians'].set_color('#DC2626')
parts['cmedians'].set_linewidth(1.5)
ax_violin.set_xticks(range(1, len(fuel_order)+1))
ax_violin.set_xticklabels(fuel_order)
ax_violin.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)')
ax_violin.set_xlabel('Fuel Type')
ax_violin.set_title('Price Density by Fuel Type (Violin Plot)')
# Add legend for mean/median
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
legend_elements = [Line2D([0], [0], color='#1F2937', linewidth=1.5, label='Mean'),
                   Line2D([0], [0], color='#DC2626', linewidth=1.5, label='Median')]
ax_violin.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='upper right', fontsize=9)
fig_violin.tight_layout()
chart_violin_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_violin)

# ── Chart 2c: Histogram per major fuel type ───────────────────────────────
major_fuels = [ft for ft in fuel_order if price_stats.loc[ft, 'count'] > 500]
fig_hist, axes_hist = plt.subplots(1, len(major_fuels), figsize=(4*len(major_fuels), 4.5), sharey=True)
if len(major_fuels) == 1:
    axes_hist = [axes_hist]
for ax, ft in zip(axes_hist, major_fuels):
    subset = df.loc[df['fuel_type'] == ft, 'price_pence']
    ax.hist(subset, bins=40, color=PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL), alpha=0.75, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5)
    ax.set_title(ft, fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    ax.set_xlabel('Price (ppl)')
    if ax == axes_hist[0]:
        ax.set_ylabel('Frequency')
fig_hist.suptitle('Price Histograms by Fuel Type', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
fig_hist.tight_layout()
chart_hist_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_hist)

# ── Section 3: Price Spread & Market Competitiveness ──────────────────────
print("\nAnalysing price spread & competitiveness...")
spread_data = price_stats[['spread', 'iqr', 'q25', 'q75']].copy()

# Chart 3a: Spread bar chart
fig_spread, ax_spread = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
x_pos = range(len(fuel_order))
bars_spread = ax_spread.bar(x_pos, spread_data.loc[fuel_order, 'spread'],
                             color=[PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL) for ft in fuel_order],
                             alpha=0.8, edgecolor='white', label='Max − Min Spread')
bars_iqr = ax_spread.bar(x_pos, spread_data.loc[fuel_order, 'iqr'],
                          color=[PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL) for ft in fuel_order],
                          alpha=0.45, edgecolor='white', label='IQR')
ax_spread.set_xticks(x_pos)
ax_spread.set_xticklabels(fuel_order)
ax_spread.set_ylabel('Price Spread (ppl)')
ax_spread.set_title('Price Spread vs Interquartile Range by Fuel Type')
ax_spread.legend()
for i, ft in enumerate(fuel_order):
    ax_spread.text(i, spread_data.loc[ft, 'spread'] + 0.5,
                   f"{spread_data.loc[ft, 'spread']:.1f}",
                   ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold')
fig_spread.tight_layout()
chart_spread_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_spread)

# Chart 3b: IQR range plot (horizontal lollipop)
fig_iqr, ax_iqr = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
for i, ft in enumerate(reversed(fuel_order)):
    q25 = spread_data.loc[ft, 'q25']
    q75 = spread_data.loc[ft, 'q75']
    med = price_stats.loc[ft, 'median']
    clr = PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL)
    ax_iqr.hlines(y=i, xmin=q25, xmax=q75, color=clr, linewidth=6, alpha=0.7)
    ax_iqr.plot(med, i, 'o', color=clr, markersize=10, zorder=5)
    ax_iqr.text(q75 + 0.5, i, f'{q25:.1f}–{q75:.1f}', va='center', fontsize=9)
ax_iqr.set_yticks(range(len(fuel_order)))
ax_iqr.set_yticklabels(list(reversed(fuel_order)))
ax_iqr.set_xlabel('Price (pence per litre)')
ax_iqr.set_title('Interquartile Range by Fuel Type (25th–75th Percentile)')
fig_iqr.tight_layout()
chart_iqr_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_iqr)

# ── Section 4: Update Freshness Analysis ──────────────────────────────────
print("\nAnalysing update freshness...")
df['update_lag_hours'] = (df['recorded_at'] - df['source_updated_at']).dt.total_seconds() / 3600

# Some lags might be negative (recorded before source_updated, which can happen with clock skew)
# or very large. We report them all but flag anomalies.
lag_stats = df.groupby('fuel_type')['update_lag_hours'].agg(
    count='count',
    mean='mean',
    median='median',
    std='std',
    min='min',
    max='max',
    q25=lambda x: x.quantile(0.25),
    q75=lambda x: x.quantile(0.75),
).sort_values('count', ascending=False)
lag_stats_display = lag_stats.copy()
for col in lag_stats_display.columns:
    if col != 'count':
        lag_stats_display[col] = lag_stats_display[col].round(2)

print(lag_stats_display)

overall_median_lag = df['update_lag_hours'].median()
overall_mean_lag = df['update_lag_hours'].mean()
pct_under_1h = (df['update_lag_hours'] < 1).mean() * 100
pct_under_24h = (df['update_lag_hours'] < 24).mean() * 100
pct_over_168h = (df['update_lag_hours'] > 168).mean() * 100  # > 1 week stale
pct_negative = (df['update_lag_hours'] < 0).mean() * 100

# Per-station freshness
station_lag = df.groupby('node_id')['update_lag_hours'].median()
stations_stale = (station_lag > 168).sum()
pct_stations_stale = stations_stale / len(station_lag) * 100

# Chart 4a: Lag distribution histogram (capped for visibility)
fig_lag, ax_lag = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
lag_capped = df['update_lag_hours'].clip(upper=500)
for ft in fuel_order:
    subset = lag_capped[df['fuel_type'] == ft]
    ax_lag.hist(subset, bins=60, alpha=0.5, color=PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL), label=ft, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.3)
ax_lag.set_xlabel('Update Lag (hours, capped at 500)')
ax_lag.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax_lag.set_title('Distribution of Update Lag by Fuel Type')
ax_lag.legend(fontsize=9)
fig_lag.tight_layout()
chart_lag_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_lag)

# Chart 4b: Lag box plot
fig_lag_box, ax_lag_box = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
lag_box_data = [df.loc[df['fuel_type'] == ft, 'update_lag_hours'].clip(upper=500).values for ft in fuel_order]
bp_lag = ax_lag_box.boxplot(lag_box_data, labels=fuel_order, patch_artist=True, showfliers=False,
                             whiskerprops=dict(linewidth=1.2),
                             medianprops=dict(linewidth=2, color='#1F2937'),
                             capprops=dict(linewidth=1.2))
for patch, ft in zip(bp_lag['boxes'], fuel_order):
    patch.set_facecolor(PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL))
    patch.set_alpha(0.7)
ax_lag_box.set_ylabel('Update Lag (hours, capped at 500)')
ax_lag_box.set_xlabel('Fuel Type')
ax_lag_box.set_title('Update Lag Distribution by Fuel Type (outliers hidden)')
fig_lag_box.tight_layout()
chart_lag_box_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_lag_box)

# Chart 4c: Lag over time (median lag by date)
df['recorded_date'] = df['recorded_at'].dt.date
lag_by_date = df.groupby('recorded_date')['update_lag_hours'].median()
fig_lag_time, ax_lag_time = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.5))
ax_lag_time.plot(lag_by_date.index, lag_by_date.values, color='#2563EB', linewidth=1.5, marker='o', markersize=3)
ax_lag_time.set_xlabel('Date')
ax_lag_time.set_ylabel('Median Update Lag (hours)')
ax_lag_time.set_title('Median Update Lag Over Time')
ax_lag_time.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=30)
fig_lag_time.tight_layout()
chart_lag_time_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_lag_time)

# ── Section 5: Station Coverage & Fuel Type Availability ──────────────────
print("\nAnalysing station coverage...")
station_fuel_count = df.groupby('node_id')['fuel_type'].nunique()
station_fuel_types = df.groupby('node_id')['fuel_type'].apply(set)

# How many fuel types per station
ft_per_station = station_fuel_count.value_counts().sort_index()
total_stations = len(station_fuel_count)

# Which fuel types have broadest coverage
fuel_station_coverage = df.groupby('fuel_type')['node_id'].nunique().sort_values(ascending=False)
fuel_station_pct = (fuel_station_coverage / total_stations * 100).round(1)

# Chart 5a: Fuel types per station (bar)
fig_ft_count, ax_ft_count = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))

ax_ft_count.set_ylabel('Number of Stations')

ax_coverage.set_yticklabels(ft_sorted)
ax_coverage.set_xlabel('Number of Stations Reporting')
ax_coverage.set_title('Station Coverage by Fuel Type')
for i, (ft, count) in enumerate(zip(ft_sorted, fuel_station_coverage.values)):
    ax_coverage.text(count + total_stations * 0.005, i, f'{count:,} ({fuel_station_pct[ft]:.1f}%)',

max_spread_ft = price_stats['spread'].idxmax()

# Finding 3: Data freshness
findings.append({

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
UK Retail Fuel Price Trend Analysis — February 2026
Report generation script: analyses data.csv and produces final_report.html
"""

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import base64
from io import BytesIO
from datetime import datetime
from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, BaseLoader
import json
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# ── Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DATA_PATH = '/app/benchmark/data.csv'
OUTPUT_DIR = '/app/output/'
REPORT_PATH = OUTPUT_DIR + 'final_report.html'

# Colour palette – professional, analytical tone
PALETTE = {
    'E10': '#2563EB',
    'B7_STANDARD': '#DC2626',
    'E5': '#059669',
    'B7_PREMIUM': '#7C3AED',
    'B10': '#D97706',
    'SDV': '#DB2777',
}
NEUTRAL = '#6B7280'
LIGHT_BG = '#F9FAFB'
GRID_CLR = '#E5E7EB'

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'sans-serif',
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.titlesize': 13,
    'axes.labelsize': 11,
    'figure.facecolor': 'white',
    'axes.facecolor': LIGHT_BG,
    'axes.grid': True,
    'grid.color': GRID_CLR,
    'grid.linewidth': 0.6,
})

# ── Helper: matplotlib figure → base64 ────────────────────────────────────
def fig_to_b64(fig, dpi=150):
    buf = BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=dpi, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
    buf.seek(0)
    b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.read()).decode('utf-8')
    plt.close(fig)
    return b64

# ── Load Data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("Loading data...")
df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH, parse_dates=['recorded_at', 'source_updated_at'])
print(f"  Records loaded: {len(df):,}")

# ── Section 1: Dataset Overview ───────────────────────────────────────────
total_records = len(df)
unique_stations = df['node_id'].nunique()
fuel_types = sorted(df['fuel_type'].unique())
date_range_start = df['recorded_at'].min()
date_range_end = df['recorded_at'].max()
date_range_str = f"{date_range_start.strftime('%d %B %Y')} – {date_range_end.strftime('%d %B %Y')}"
null_counts = df.isnull().sum().to_dict()

fuel_type_counts = df.groupby('fuel_type').size().sort_values(ascending=False).to_dict()

print(f"  Unique stations: {unique_stations:,}")
print(f"  Fuel types: {fuel_types}")
print(f"  Date range: {date_range_str}")

# ── Section 2: Price Distribution by Fuel Type ────────────────────────────
print("\nAnalysing price distributions...")
price_stats = df.groupby('fuel_type')['price_pence'].agg(
    count='count',
    mean='mean',
    median='median',
    std='std',
    min='min',
    max='max',
    q25=lambda x: x.quantile(0.25),
    q75=lambda x: x.quantile(0.75),
).sort_values('count', ascending=False)
price_stats['iqr'] = price_stats['q75'] - price_stats['q25']
price_stats['spread'] = price_stats['max'] - price_stats['min']

# Round for display
price_stats_display = price_stats.copy()
for col in ['mean', 'median', 'std', 'min', 'max', 'q25', 'q75', 'iqr', 'spread']:
    price_stats_display[col] = price_stats_display[col].round(1)

print(price_stats_display[['count', 'mean', 'median', 'std', 'min', 'max', 'iqr', 'spread']])

# ── Chart 2a: Box plot of price by fuel type ──────────────────────────────
fuel_order = price_stats.index.tolist()
fig_box, ax_box = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
box_data = [df.loc[df['fuel_type'] == ft, 'price_pence'].values for ft in fuel_order]
bp = ax_box.boxplot(box_data, labels=fuel_order, patch_artist=True, showfliers=True,
                    flierprops=dict(marker='o', markersize=2, alpha=0.3),
                    whiskerprops=dict(linewidth=1.2),
                    medianprops=dict(linewidth=2, color='#1F2937'),
                    capprops=dict(linewidth=1.2))
for patch, ft in zip(bp['boxes'], fuel_order):
    patch.set_facecolor(PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL))
    patch.set_alpha(0.7)
ax_box.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)')
ax_box.set_xlabel('Fuel Type')
ax_box.set_title('Price Distribution by Fuel Type')
ax_box.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FormatStrFormatter('%d'))
fig_box.tight_layout()
chart_box_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_box)

# ── Chart 2b: Violin plot ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig_violin, ax_violin = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
parts = ax_violin.violinplot(box_data, positions=range(1, len(fuel_order)+1),
                              showmeans=True, showmedians=True, showextrema=False)
for i, pc in enumerate(parts['bodies']):
    pc.set_facecolor(PALETTE.get(fuel_order[i], NEUTRAL))
    pc.set_alpha(0.6)
parts['cmeans'].set_color('#1F2937')
parts['cmeans'].set_linewidth(1.5)
parts['cmedians'].set_color('#DC2626')
parts['cmedians'].set_linewidth(1.5)
ax_violin.set_xticks(range(1, len(fuel_order)+1))
ax_violin.set_xticklabels(fuel_order)
ax_violin.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)')
ax_violin.set_xlabel('Fuel Type')
ax_violin.set_title('Price Density by Fuel Type (Violin Plot)')
# Add legend for mean/median
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
legend_elements = [Line2D([0], [0], color='#1F2937', linewidth=1.5, label='Mean'),
                   Line2D([0], [0], color='#DC2626', linewidth=1.5, label='Median')]
ax_violin.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='upper right', fontsize=9)
fig_violin.tight_layout()
chart_violin_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_violin)

# ── Chart 2c: Histogram per major fuel type ───────────────────────────────
major_fuels = [ft for ft in fuel_order if price_stats.loc[ft, 'count'] > 500]
fig_hist, axes_hist = plt.subplots(1, len(major_fuels), figsize=(4*len(major_fuels), 4.5), sharey=True)
if len(major_fuels) == 1:
    axes_hist = [axes_hist]
for ax, ft in zip(axes_hist, major_fuels):
    subset = df.loc[df['fuel_type'] == ft, 'price_pence']
    ax.hist(subset, bins=40, color=PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL), alpha=0.75, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5)
    ax.set_title(ft, fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    ax.set_xlabel('Price (ppl)')
    if ax == axes_hist[0]:
        ax.set_ylabel('Frequency')
fig_hist.suptitle('Price Histograms by Fuel Type', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
fig_hist.tight_layout()
chart_hist_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_hist)

# ── Section 3: Price Spread & Market Competitiveness ──────────────────────
print("\nAnalysing price spread & competitiveness...")
spread_data = price_stats[['spread', 'iqr', 'q25', 'q75']].copy()

# Chart 3a: Spread bar chart
fig_spread, ax_spread = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
x_pos = range(len(fuel_order))
bars_spread = ax_spread.bar(x_pos, spread_data.loc[fuel_order, 'spread'],
                             color=[PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL) for ft in fuel_order],
                             alpha=0.8, edgecolor='white', label='Max − Min Spread')
bars_iqr = ax_spread.bar(x_pos, spread_data.loc[fuel_order, 'iqr'],
                          color=[PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL) for ft in fuel_order],
                          alpha=0.45, edgecolor='white', label='IQR')
ax_spread.set_xticks(x_pos)
ax_spread.set_xticklabels(fuel_order)
ax_spread.set_ylabel('Price Spread (ppl)')
ax_spread.set_title('Price Spread vs Interquartile Range by Fuel Type')
ax_spread.legend()
for i, ft in enumerate(fuel_order):
    ax_spread.text(i, spread_data.loc[ft, 'spread'] + 0.5,
                   f"{spread_data.loc[ft, 'spread']:.1f}",
                   ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold')
fig_spread.tight_layout()
chart_spread_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_spread)

# Chart 3b: IQR range plot (horizontal lollipop)
fig_iqr, ax_iqr = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
for i, ft in enumerate(reversed(fuel_order)):
    q25 = spread_data.loc[ft, 'q25']
    q75 = spread_data.loc[ft, 'q75']
    med = price_stats.loc[ft, 'median']
    clr = PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL)
    ax_iqr.hlines(y=i, xmin=q25, xmax=q75, color=clr, linewidth=6, alpha=0.7)
    ax_iqr.plot(med, i, 'o', color=clr, markersize=10, zorder=5)
    ax_iqr.text(q75 + 0.5, i, f'{q25:.1f}–{q75:.1f}', va='center', fontsize=9)
ax_iqr.set_yticks(range(len(fuel_order)))
ax_iqr.set_yticklabels(list(reversed(fuel_order)))
ax_iqr.set_xlabel('Price (pence per litre)')
ax_iqr.set_title('Interquartile Range by Fuel Type (25th–75th Percentile)')
fig_iqr.tight_layout()
chart_iqr_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_iqr)

# ── Section 4: Update Freshness Analysis ──────────────────────────────────
print("\nAnalysing update freshness...")
df['update_lag_hours'] = (df['recorded_at'] - df['source_updated_at']).dt.total_seconds() / 3600

# Some lags might be negative (recorded before source_updated, which can happen with clock skew)
# or very large. We report them all but flag anomalies.
lag_stats = df.groupby('fuel_type')['update_lag_hours'].agg(
    count='count',
    mean='mean',
    median='median',
    std='std',
    min='min',
    max='max',
    q25=lambda x: x.quantile(0.25),
    q75=lambda x: x.quantile(0.75),
).sort_values('count', ascending=False)
lag_stats_display = lag_stats.copy()
for col in lag_stats_display.columns:
    if col != 'count':
        lag_stats_display[col] = lag_stats_display[col].round(2)

print(lag_stats_display)

overall_median_lag = df['update_lag_hours'].median()
overall_mean_lag = df['update_lag_hours'].mean()
pct_under_1h = (df['update_lag_hours'] < 1).mean() * 100
pct_under_24h = (df['update_lag_hours'] < 24).mean() * 100
pct_over_168h = (df['update_lag_hours'] > 168).mean() * 100  # > 1 week stale
pct_negative = (df['update_lag_hours'] < 0).mean() * 100

# Per-station freshness
station_lag = df.groupby('node_id')['update_lag_hours'].median()
stations_stale = (station_lag > 168).sum()
pct_stations_stale = stations_stale / len(station_lag) * 100

# Chart 4a: Lag distribution histogram (capped for visibility)
fig_lag, ax_lag = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
lag_capped = df['update_lag_hours'].clip(upper=500)
for ft in fuel_order:
    subset = lag_capped[df['fuel_type'] == ft]
    ax_lag.hist(subset, bins=60, alpha=0.5, color=PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL), label=ft, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.3)
ax_lag.set_xlabel('Update Lag (hours, capped at 500)')
ax_lag.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax_lag.set_title('Distribution of Update Lag by Fuel Type')
ax_lag.legend(fontsize=9)
fig_lag.tight_layout()
chart_lag_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_lag)

# Chart 4b: Lag box plot
fig_lag_box, ax_lag_box = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
lag_box_data = [df.loc[df['fuel_type'] == ft, 'update_lag_hours'].clip(upper=500).values for ft in fuel_order]
bp_lag = ax_lag_box.boxplot(lag_box_data, labels=fuel_order, patch_artist=True, showfliers=False,
                             whiskerprops=dict(linewidth=1.2),
                             medianprops=dict(linewidth=2, color='#1F2937'),
                             capprops=dict(linewidth=1.2))
for patch, ft in zip(bp_lag['boxes'], fuel_order):
    patch.set_facecolor(PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL))
    patch.set_alpha(0.7)
ax_lag_box.set_ylabel('Update Lag (hours, capped at 500)')
ax_lag_box.set_xlabel('Fuel Type')
ax_lag_box.set_title('Update Lag Distribution by Fuel Type (outliers hidden)')
fig_lag_box.tight_layout()
chart_lag_box_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_lag_box)

# Chart 4c: Lag over time (median lag by date)
df['recorded_date'] = df['recorded_at'].dt.date
lag_by_date = df.groupby('recorded_date')['update_lag_hours'].median()
fig_lag_time, ax_lag_time = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.5))
ax_lag_time.plot(lag_by_date.index, lag_by_date.values, color='#2563EB', linewidth=1.5, marker='o', markersize=3)
ax_lag_time.set_xlabel('Date')
ax_lag_time.set_ylabel('Median Update Lag (hours)')
ax_lag_time.set_title('Median Update Lag Over Time')
ax_lag_time.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=30)
fig_lag_time.tight_layout()
chart_lag_time_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_lag_time)

# ── Section 5: Station Coverage & Fuel Type Availability ──────────────────
print("\nAnalysing station coverage...")
station_fuel_count = df.groupby('node_id')['fuel_type'].nunique()
station_fuel_types = df.groupby('node_id')['fuel_type'].apply(set)

# How many fuel types per station
ft_per_station = station_fuel_count.value_counts().sort_index()
total_stations = len(station_fuel_count)

# Which fuel types have broadest coverage
fuel_station_coverage = df.groupby('fuel_type')['node_id'].nunique().sort_values(ascending=False)
fuel_station_pct = (fuel_station_coverage / total_stations * 100).round(1)

# Chart 5a: Fuel types per station (bar)
fig_ft_count, ax_ft_count = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))
ax_ft_count.bar(ft_per_station.index, ft_per_station.values, color='#2563EB', alpha=0.8, edgecolor='white')
ax_ft_count.set_xlabel('Number of Fuel Types Reported')
ax_ft_count.set_ylabel('Number of Stations')
ax_ft_count.set_title('Distribution of Fuel Types per Station')
for i, (k, v) in enumerate(ft_per_station.items()):
    ax_ft_count.text(k, v + total_stations * 0.005, f'{v:,}', ha='center', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold')
fig_ft_count.tight_layout()
chart_ft_count_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_ft_count)

# Chart 5b: Station coverage by fuel type (horizontal bar)
fig_coverage, ax_coverage = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
ft_sorted = fuel_station_coverage.index.tolist()
y_pos = range(len(ft_sorted))
ax_coverage.barh(y_pos, fuel_station_coverage.values,
                 color=[PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL) for ft in ft_sorted], alpha=0.8, edgecolor='white')
ax_coverage.set_yticks(y_pos)
ax_coverage.set_yticklabels(ft_sorted)
ax_coverage.set_xlabel('Number of Stations Reporting')
ax_coverage.set_title('Station Coverage by Fuel Type')
for i, (ft, count) in enumerate(zip(ft_sorted, fuel_station_coverage.values)):
    ax_coverage.text(count + total_stations * 0.005, i, f'{count:,} ({fuel_station_pct[ft]:.1f}%)',
                     va='center', fontsize=9)
fig_coverage.tight_layout()
chart_coverage_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_coverage)

# ── Section 6: Key Findings & Policy Implications ─────────────────────────
# Synthesize findings
findings = []

# Finding 1: Most/least expensive fuel type
most_expensive = price_stats['mean'].idxmax()
least_expensive = price_stats['mean'].idxmin()
findings.append({
    'num': 1,
    'title': f'{most_expensive} is the most expensive fuel type, {least_expensive} the cheapest',
    'detail': (
        f"The average price of {most_expensive} is {price_stats.loc[most_expensive, 'mean']:.1f} ppl, "
        f"compared to {least_expensive} at {price_stats.loc[least_expensive, 'mean']:.1f} ppl — "
        f"a difference of {price_stats.loc[most_expensive, 'mean'] - price_stats.loc[least_expensive, 'mean']:.1f} ppl. "
        f"Premium diesel ({most_expensive}) commands a substantial premium over standard fuels, "
        f"which is expected but the magnitude warrants monitoring."
    ),
    'implication': 'Policy focus should be on ensuring premium fuel pricing is transparent and that consumers are not inadvertently purchasing premium grades at inflated margins.'
})

# Finding 2: Price spread
max_spread_ft = price_stats['spread'].idxmax()
findings.append({
    'num': 2,
    'title': f'Significant price disparities exist within fuel types, especially {max_spread_ft}',
    'detail': (
        f"The price spread (max − min) for {max_spread_ft} is {price_stats.loc[max_spread_ft, 'spread']:.1f} ppl. "
        f"Even for the most common fuel types, the IQR indicates consumers in the middle 50% of stations "
        f"face a price band of {price_stats.loc['E10', 'iqr']:.1f} ppl (E10) to "
        f"{price_stats.loc['B7_STANDARD', 'iqr']:.1f} ppl (B7_STANDARD). "
        f"This means a typical motorist filling 50 litres could pay £{price_stats.loc['E10', 'iqr']*50/100:.2f}–£{price_stats.loc['B7_STANDARD', 'iqr']*50/100:.2f} "
        f"more depending on which station they visit."
    ),
    'implication': 'These disparities suggest either local market power or information asymmetry. Strengthening price transparency tools and promoting real-time comparison could improve consumer outcomes.'
})

# Finding 3: Data freshness
findings.append({
    'num': 3,
    'title': f'Most price updates are timely, but a notable tail of stale data exists',
    'detail': (
        f"The median update lag is {overall_median_lag:.1f} hours. "
        f"{pct_under_1h:.1f}% of records have a lag under 1 hour, and {pct_under_24h:.1f}% under 24 hours. "
        f"However, {pct_over_168h:.1f}% of records have lags exceeding one week, "
        f"and {pct_stations_stale:.1f}% of stations ({stations_stale:,} of {total_stations:,}) "
        f"have a median lag over 168 hours. "
        f"{'Negative lags (recorded before source update) affect ' + f'{pct_negative:.2f}% of records, suggesting minor clock synchronisation issues. ' if pct_negative > 0 else ''}"
        f"This indicates a subset of retailers are not updating their feeds promptly."
    ),
    'implication': 'The government should consider enforcement mechanisms for timely price reporting, as stale data undermines the purpose of the open data scheme and disadvantages consumers relying on price comparison tools.'
})

# Finding 4: Coverage
least_covered = fuel_station_coverage.idxmin()

findings.append({
    'num': 4,
    'title': f'Fuel type coverage varies significantly across stations',
    'detail': (
        f"{most_covered} is reported by {fuel_station_coverage[most_covered]:,} stations "
        f"({fuel_station_pct[most_covered]:.1f}%), while {least_covered} is only reported by "

        f"report only a single fuel type, limiting comparison for consumers with specific fuel needs."
    ),
    'implication': 'Mandating broader fuel type reporting could improve market transparency, especially for consumers using alternative or premium fuels.'
})

# Finding 5: E10 vs B7_STANDARD comparison
if 'E10' in price_stats.index and 'B7_STANDARD' in price_stats.index:
    diesel_premium = price_stats.loc['B7_STANDARD', 'mean'] - price_stats.loc['E10', 'mean']
    findings.append({
        'num': 5,
        'title': f'Diesel (B7) carries a {"premium" if diesel_premium > 0 else "discount"} over unleaded (E10)',
        'detail': (
            f"B7_STANDARD averages {price_stats.loc['B7_STANDARD', 'mean']:.1f} ppl vs "
            f"E10 at {price_stats.loc['E10', 'mean']:.1f} ppl — "
            f"a difference of {abs(diesel_premium):.1f} ppl. "
            f"This {'premium' if diesel_premium > 0 else 'discount'} is consistent with wholesale market "
            f"dynamics but the retail margin spread warrants continued monitoring."
        ),
        'implication': 'Tracking the diesel-unleaded price differential over time can reveal whether retailers pass through wholesale cost changes symmetrically or exercise pricing power.'
    })

# ── Render HTML Report ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("\nGenerating HTML report...")

html_template = r"""<!DOCTYPE html>

<header class="report-header">

The dataset comprises <strong>{{ "{:,}".format(total_records) }}</strong> individual price observations across <strong>{{ "{:,}".format(unique_stations) }}</strong> unique stations (anonymised via hashed identifiers).</p>

A wide spread suggests that consumers face significantly different prices depending on which forecourt they visit — potentially indicating local market power or information asymmetry.</p>

    <h3>Key Spread Metrics</h3>
    <table>
      <thead><tr><th>Fuel Type</th><th>IQR (ppl)</th><th>25th %ile</th><th>Median</th><th>75th %ile</th><th>Max − Min</th></tr></thead>

For E10 (standard unleaded), the typical price range of {{ "%.1f"|format(spread_data.loc['E10', 'q25']) }}–{{ "%.1f"|format(spread_data.loc['E10', 'q75']) }} ppl means that a consumer filling 50 litres could see a difference of <strong>£{{ "%.2f"|format(spread_data.loc['E10', 'iqr'] * 50 / 100) }}</strong> between a typical lower-quartile and upper-quartile station. The max−min spread is far wider, indicating extreme outliers that merit investigation.</p>

Stale pricing data undermines the government's open data scheme and disadvantages consumers who rely on price comparison tools.</p>

These have been retained in the analysis but flagged as anomalous.</div>

    <p>An estimated <strong>{{ stations_stale:, }}</strong> stations ({{ "%.1f"|format(pct_stations_stale) }}% of all stations) have a median update lag exceeding one week (168 hours). These stations represent a compliance risk for the open data scheme.</p>
  </section>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
UK Retail Fuel Price Trend Analysis — February 2026
Report generation script: analyses data.csv and produces final_report.html
"""

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import base64
from io import BytesIO
from datetime import datetime
from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, BaseLoader
import json
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# ── Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DATA_PATH = '/app/benchmark/data.csv'
OUTPUT_DIR = '/app/output/'
REPORT_PATH = OUTPUT_DIR + 'final_report.html'

# Colour palette – professional, analytical tone
PALETTE = {
    'E10': '#2563EB',
    'B7_STANDARD': '#DC2626',
    'E5': '#059669',
    'B7_PREMIUM': '#7C3AED',
    'B10': '#D97706',
    'SDV': '#DB2777',
}
NEUTRAL = '#6B7280'
LIGHT_BG = '#F9FAFB'
GRID_CLR = '#E5E7EB'

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'sans-serif',
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.titlesize': 13,
    'axes.labelsize': 11,
    'figure.facecolor': 'white',
    'axes.facecolor': LIGHT_BG,
    'axes.grid': True,
    'grid.color': GRID_CLR,
    'grid.linewidth': 0.6,
})

# ── Helper: matplotlib figure → base64 ────────────────────────────────────
def fig_to_b64(fig, dpi=150):
    buf = BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=dpi, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
    buf.seek(0)
    b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.read()).decode('utf-8')
    plt.close(fig)
    return b64

# ── Load Data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("Loading data...")
df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH, parse_dates=['recorded_at', 'source_updated_at'])
print(f"  Records loaded: {len(df):,}")

# ── Section 1: Dataset Overview ───────────────────────────────────────────
total_records = len(df)
unique_stations = df['node_id'].nunique()
fuel_types = sorted(df['fuel_type'].unique())
date_range_start = df['recorded_at'].min()
date_range_end = df['recorded_at'].max()
date_range_str = f"{date_range_start.strftime('%d %B %Y')} – {date_range_end.strftime('%d %B %Y')}"
null_counts = df.isnull().sum().to_dict()

fuel_type_counts = df.groupby('fuel_type').size().sort_values(ascending=False).to_dict()

print(f"  Unique stations: {unique_stations:,}")
print(f"  Fuel types: {fuel_types}")
print(f"  Date range: {date_range_str}")

# ── Section 2: Price Distribution by Fuel Type ────────────────────────────
print("\nAnalysing price distributions...")
price_stats = df.groupby('fuel_type')['price_pence'].agg(
    count='count',
    mean='mean',
    median='median',
    std='std',
    min='min',
    max='max',
    q25=lambda x: x.quantile(0.25),
    q75=lambda x: x.quantile(0.75),
).sort_values('count', ascending=False)
price_stats['iqr'] = price_stats['q75'] - price_stats['q25']
price_stats['spread'] = price_stats['max'] - price_stats['min']

# Round for display
price_stats_display = price_stats.copy()
for col in ['mean', 'median', 'std', 'min', 'max', 'q25', 'q75', 'iqr', 'spread']:
    price_stats_display[col] = price_stats_display[col].round(1)

print(price_stats_display[['count', 'mean', 'median', 'std', 'min', 'max', 'iqr', 'spread']])

# ── Chart 2a: Box plot of price by fuel type ──────────────────────────────
fuel_order = price_stats.index.tolist()
fig_box, ax_box = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
box_data = [df.loc[df['fuel_type'] == ft, 'price_pence'].values for ft in fuel_order]
bp = ax_box.boxplot(box_data, labels=fuel_order, patch_artist=True, showfliers=True,
                    flierprops=dict(marker='o', markersize=2, alpha=0.3),
                    whiskerprops=dict(linewidth=1.2),
                    medianprops=dict(linewidth=2, color='#1F2937'),
                    capprops=dict(linewidth=1.2))
for patch, ft in zip(bp['boxes'], fuel_order):
    patch.set_facecolor(PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL))
    patch.set_alpha(0.7)
ax_box.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)')
ax_box.set_xlabel('Fuel Type')
ax_box.set_title('Price Distribution by Fuel Type')
ax_box.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FormatStrFormatter('%d'))
fig_box.tight_layout()
chart_box_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_box)

# ── Chart 2b: Violin plot ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig_violin, ax_violin = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
parts = ax_violin.violinplot(box_data, positions=range(1, len(fuel_order)+1),

overall_median_lag = df['update_lag_hours'].median()

pct_under_24h = (df['update_lag_hours'] < 24).mean() * 100

pct_negative = (df['update_lag_hours'] < 0).mean() * 100

ax_lag.legend(fontsize=9)
fig_lag.tight_layout()

# Chart 4b: Lag box plot
fig_lag_box, ax_lag_box = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
lag_box_data = [df.loc[df['fuel_type'] == ft, 'update_lag_hours'].clip(upper=500).values for ft in fuel_order]
bp_lag = ax_lag_box.boxplot(lag_box_data, labels=fuel_order, patch_artist=True, showfliers=False,
                             whiskerprops=dict(linewidth=1.2),
                             medianprops=dict(linewidth=2, color='#1F2937'),
                             capprops=dict(linewidth=1.2))
for patch, ft in zip(bp_lag['boxes'], fuel_order):
    patch.set_facecolor(PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL))
    patch.set_alpha(0.7)
ax_lag_box.set_ylabel('Update Lag (hours, capped at 500)')
ax_lag_box.set_xlabel('Fuel Type')
ax_lag_box.set_title('Update Lag Distribution by Fuel Type (outliers hidden)')
fig_lag_box.tight_layout()
chart_lag_box_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_lag_box)

# Chart 4c: Lag over time (median lag by date)
df['recorded_date'] = df['recorded_at'].dt.date
lag_by_date = df.groupby('recorded_date')['update_lag_hours'].median()
fig_lag_time, ax_lag_time = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.5))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
UK Retail Fuel Price Trend Analysis — February 2026
Report generation script: analyses data.csv and produces final_report.html
"""

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import base64
from io import BytesIO
from datetime import datetime
from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, BaseLoader
import json
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# ── Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DATA_PATH = '/app/benchmark/data.csv'
OUTPUT_DIR = '/app/output/'
REPORT_PATH = OUTPUT_DIR + 'final_report.html'

# Colour palette – professional, analytical tone
PALETTE = {
    'E10': '#2563EB',
    'B7_STANDARD': '#DC2626',
    'E5': '#059669',
    'B7_PREMIUM': '#7C3AED',
    'B10': '#D97706',
    'SDV': '#DB2777',
}
NEUTRAL = '#6B7280'
LIGHT_BG = '#F9FAFB'
GRID_CLR = '#E5E7EB'

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'sans-serif',
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.titlesize': 13,
    'axes.labelsize': 11,
    'figure.facecolor': 'white',
    'axes.facecolor': LIGHT_BG,
    'axes.grid': True,
    'grid.color': GRID_CLR,
    'grid.linewidth': 0.6,
})

# ── Helper: matplotlib figure → base64 ────────────────────────────────────
def fig_to_b64(fig, dpi=150):
    buf = BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=dpi, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
    buf.seek(0)
    b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.read()).decode('utf-8')
    plt.close(fig)
    return b64

# ── Load Data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("Loading data...")
df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH, parse_dates=['recorded_at', 'source_updated_at'])
print(f"  Records loaded: {len(df):,}")

# ── Section 1: Dataset Overview ───────────────────────────────────────────
total_records = len(df)
unique_stations = df['node_id'].nunique()
fuel_types = sorted(df['fuel_type'].unique())
date_range_start = df['recorded_at'].min()
date_range_end = df['recorded_at'].max()
date_range_str = f"{date_range_start.strftime('%d %B %Y')} – {date_range_end.strftime('%d %B %Y')}"
null_counts = df.isnull().sum().to_dict()

fuel_type_counts = df.groupby('fuel_type').size().sort_values(ascending=False).to_dict()

print(f"  Unique stations: {unique_stations:,}")
print(f"  Fuel types: {fuel_types}")
print(f"  Date range: {date_range_str}")

# ── Section 2: Price Distribution by Fuel Type ────────────────────────────
print("\nAnalysing price distributions...")
price_stats = df.groupby('fuel_type')['price_pence'].agg(
    count='count',
    mean='mean',
    median='median',
    std='std',
    min='min',
    max='max',
    q25=lambda x: x.quantile(0.25),
    q75=lambda x: x.quantile(0.75),
).sort_values('count', ascending=False)
price_stats['iqr'] = price_stats['q75'] - price_stats['q25']
price_stats['spread'] = price_stats['max'] - price_stats['min']

# Round for display
price_stats_display = price_stats.copy()
for col in ['mean', 'median', 'std', 'min', 'max', 'q25', 'q75', 'iqr', 'spread']:
    price_stats_display[col] = price_stats_display[col].round(1)

print(price_stats_display[['count', 'mean', 'median', 'std', 'min', 'max', 'iqr', 'spread']])

# ── Chart 2a: Box plot of price by fuel type ──────────────────────────────
fuel_order = price_stats.index.tolist()
fig_box, ax_box = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
box_data = [df.loc[df['fuel_type'] == ft, 'price_pence'].values for ft in fuel_order]
bp = ax_box.boxplot(box_data, labels=fuel_order, patch_artist=True, showfliers=True,
                    flierprops=dict(marker='o', markersize=2, alpha=0.3),
                    whiskerprops=dict(linewidth=1.2),
                    medianprops=dict(linewidth=2, color='#1F2937'),
                    capprops=dict(linewidth=1.2))
for patch, ft in zip(bp['boxes'], fuel_order):
    patch.set_facecolor(PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL))
    patch.set_alpha(0.7)
ax_box.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)')
ax_box.set_xlabel('Fuel Type')
ax_box.set_title('Price Distribution by Fuel Type')
ax_box.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FormatStrFormatter('%d'))
fig_box.tight_layout()
chart_box_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_box)

# ── Chart 2b: Violin plot ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig_violin, ax_violin = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
parts = ax_violin.violinplot(box_data, positions=range(1, len(fuel_order)+1),
                              showmeans=True, showmedians=True, showextrema=False)
for i, pc in enumerate(parts['bodies']):
    pc.set_facecolor(PALETTE.get(fuel_order[i], NEUTRAL))
    pc.set_alpha(0.6)
parts['cmeans'].set_color('#1F2937')
parts['cmeans'].set_linewidth(1.5)
parts['cmedians'].set_color('#DC2626')
parts['cmedians'].set_linewidth(1.5)
ax_violin.set_xticks(range(1, len(fuel_order)+1))
ax_violin.set_xticklabels(fuel_order)
ax_violin.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)')
ax_violin.set_xlabel('Fuel Type')
ax_violin.set_title('Price Density by Fuel Type (Violin Plot)')
# Add legend for mean/median
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
legend_elements = [Line2D([0], [0], color='#1F2937', linewidth=1.5, label='Mean'),
                   Line2D([0], [0], color='#DC2626', linewidth=1.5, label='Median')]
ax_violin.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='upper right', fontsize=9)
fig_violin.tight_layout()
chart_violin_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_violin)

# ── Chart 2c: Histogram per major fuel type ───────────────────────────────
major_fuels = [ft for ft in fuel_order if price_stats.loc[ft, 'count'] > 500]
fig_hist, axes_hist = plt.subplots(1, len(major_fuels), figsize=(4*len(major_fuels), 4.5), sharey=True)
if len(major_fuels) == 1:
    axes_hist = [axes_hist]
for ax, ft in zip(axes_hist, major_fuels):
    subset = df.loc[df['fuel_type'] == ft, 'price_pence']
    ax.hist(subset, bins=40, color=PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL), alpha=0.75, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5)
    ax.set_title(ft, fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    ax.set_xlabel('Price (ppl)')
    if ax == axes_hist[0]:
        ax.set_ylabel('Frequency')
fig_hist.suptitle('Price Histograms by Fuel Type', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
fig_hist.tight_layout()
chart_hist_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_hist)

# ── Section 3: Price Spread & Market Competitiveness ──────────────────────
print("\nAnalysing price spread & competitiveness...")
spread_data = price_stats[['spread', 'iqr', 'q25', 'q75']].copy()

# Chart 3a: Spread bar chart
fig_spread, ax_spread = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
x_pos = range(len(fuel_order))
bars_spread = ax_spread.bar(x_pos, spread_data.loc[fuel_order, 'spread'],
                             color=[PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL) for ft in fuel_order],
                             alpha=0.8, edgecolor='white', label='Max − Min Spread')
bars_iqr = ax_spread.bar(x_pos, spread_data.loc[fuel_order, 'iqr'],
                          color=[PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL) for ft in fuel_order],
                          alpha=0.45, edgecolor='white', label='IQR')
ax_spread.set_xticks(x_pos)
ax_spread.set_xticklabels(fuel_order)
ax_spread.set_ylabel('Price Spread (ppl)')
ax_spread.set_title('Price Spread vs Interquartile Range by Fuel Type')
ax_spread.legend()
for i, ft in enumerate(fuel_order):
    ax_spread.text(i, spread_data.loc[ft, 'spread'] + 0.5,
                   f"{spread_data.loc[ft, 'spread']:.1f}",
                   ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold')
fig_spread.tight_layout()
chart_spread_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_spread)

# Chart 3b: IQR range plot (horizontal lollipop)
fig_iqr, ax_iqr = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
for i, ft in enumerate(reversed(fuel_order)):
    q25 = spread_data.loc[ft, 'q25']
    q75 = spread_data.loc[ft, 'q75']
    med = price_stats.loc[ft, 'median']
    clr = PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL)
    ax_iqr.hlines(y=i, xmin=q25, xmax=q75, color=clr, linewidth=6, alpha=0.7)
    ax_iqr.plot(med, i, 'o', color=clr, markersize=10, zorder=5)
    ax_iqr.text(q75 + 0.5, i, f'{q25:.1f}–{q75:.1f}', va='center', fontsize=9)
ax_iqr.set_yticks(range(len(fuel_order)))
ax_iqr.set_yticklabels(list(reversed(fuel_order)))
ax_iqr.set_xlabel('Price (pence per litre)')
ax_iqr.set_title('Interquartile Range by Fuel Type (25th–75th Percentile)')
fig_iqr.tight_layout()
chart_iqr_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_iqr)

# ── Section 4: Update Freshness Analysis ──────────────────────────────────
print("\nAnalysing update freshness...")
df['update_lag_hours'] = (df['recorded_at'] - df['source_updated_at']).dt.total_seconds() / 3600

# Some lags might be negative (recorded before source_updated, which can happen with clock skew)
# or very large. We report them all but flag anomalies.
lag_stats = df.groupby('fuel_type')['update_lag_hours'].agg(
    count='count',
    mean='mean',
    median='median',
    std='std',
    min='min',
    max='max',
    q25=lambda x: x.quantile(0.25),
    q75=lambda x: x.quantile(0.75),
).sort_values('count', ascending=False)
lag_stats_display = lag_stats.copy()
for col in lag_stats_display.columns:
    if col != 'count':
        lag_stats_display[col] = lag_stats_display[col].round(2)

print(lag_stats_display)

overall_median_lag = df['update_lag_hours'].median()
overall_mean_lag = df['update_lag_hours'].mean()
pct_under_1h = (df['update_lag_hours'] < 1).mean() * 100
pct_under_24h = (df['update_lag_hours'] < 24).mean() * 100
pct_over_168h = (df['update_lag_hours'] > 168).mean() * 100  # > 1 week stale
pct_negative = (df['update_lag_hours'] < 0).mean() * 100

# Per-station freshness
station_lag = df.groupby('node_id')['update_lag_hours'].median()
stations_stale = (station_lag > 168).sum()
pct_stations_stale = stations_stale / len(station_lag) * 100

# Chart 4a: Lag distribution histogram (capped for visibility)
fig_lag, ax_lag = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
lag_capped = df['update_lag_hours'].clip(upper=500)
for ft in fuel_order:
    subset = lag_capped[df['fuel_type'] == ft]
    ax_lag.hist(subset, bins=60, alpha=0.5, color=PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL), label=ft, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.3)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
UK Retail Fuel Price Trend Analysis — February 2026
Report generation script: analyses data.csv and produces final_report.html
"""

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import base64
from io import BytesIO
from datetime import datetime
from jinja2 import Environment, BaseLoader
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# ── Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DATA_PATH = '/app/benchmark/data.csv'
OUTPUT_DIR = '/app/output/'
REPORT_PATH = OUTPUT_DIR + 'final_report.html'

PALETTE = {
    'E10': '#2563EB',
    'B7_STANDARD': '#DC2626',
    'E5': '#059669',
    'B7_PREMIUM': '#7C3AED',
    'B10': '#D97706',
    'HVO': '#DB2777',
}
NEUTRAL = '#6B7280'
LIGHT_BG = '#F9FAFB'
GRID_CLR = '#E5E7EB'

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'sans-serif',
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.titlesize': 13,
    'axes.labelsize': 11,
    'figure.facecolor': 'white',
    'axes.facecolor': LIGHT_BG,
    'axes.grid': True,
    'grid.color': GRID_CLR,
    'grid.linewidth': 0.6,
})


def fig_to_b64(fig, dpi=150):
    buf = BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format='png', dpi=dpi, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
    buf.seek(0)
    b64 = base64.b64encode(buf.read()).decode('utf-8')
    plt.close(fig)
    return b64


def pct_str(val, decimals=1):
    """Format a value as percentage string without using % in Jinja2."""
    fmt = "{{:.{}f}}".format(decimals)
    return fmt.format(val) + " pct"


def fmt1(val):
    return f"{val:.1f}"


def fmt2(val):
    return f"{val:.2f}"


def fmti(val):
    return f"{val:,}"


# ── Load Data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("Loading data...")
df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH, parse_dates=['recorded_at', 'source_updated_at'])
total_records = len(df)
print(f"  Records: {total_records:,}")

# ── Section 1: Dataset Overview ───────────────────────────────────────────
unique_stations = df['node_id'].nunique()
fuel_types = sorted(df['fuel_type'].unique())
date_range_start = df['recorded_at'].min()
date_range_end = df['recorded_at'].max()
date_range_str = f"{date_range_start.strftime('%d %B %Y')} – {date_range_end.strftime('%d %B %Y')}"
date_span_days = (date_range_end - date_range_start).days
null_counts = df.isnull().sum().to_dict()
fuel_type_counts = df.groupby('fuel_type').size().sort_values(ascending=False).to_dict()

# Outlier detection — flag prices outside plausible UK fuel range
LOW_THRESH = 100   # below 100 ppl is almost certainly erroneous
HIGH_THRESH = 250  # above 250 ppl for standard fuels is highly suspicious
outlier_low = df[df['price_pence'] < LOW_THRESH]
outlier_high = df[df['price_pence'] > HIGH_THRESH]
n_outlier_low = len(outlier_low)
n_outlier_high = len(outlier_high)

fuel_type_descriptions = {
    'E10': 'Standard unleaded petrol (up to 10% ethanol)',
    'B7_STANDARD': 'Standard diesel (up to 7% biodiesel)',
    'E5': 'Super unleaded petrol (up to 5% ethanol)',
    'B7_PREMIUM': 'Premium diesel',
    'B10': 'B10 biodiesel blend',
    'HVO': 'Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil diesel',
}

# ── Section 2: Price Distribution by Fuel Type ────────────────────────────
print("Analysing price distributions...")
price_stats = df.groupby('fuel_type')['price_pence'].agg(
    count='count',
    mean='mean',
    median='median',
    std='std',
    min='min',
    max='max',
    q25=lambda x: x.quantile(0.25),
    q75=lambda x: x.quantile(0.75),
).sort_values('count', ascending=False)
price_stats['iqr'] = price_stats['q75'] - price_stats['q25']
price_stats['spread'] = price_stats['max'] - price_stats['min']
fuel_order = price_stats.index.tolist()

# Chart 2a: Box plot
box_data = [df.loc[df['fuel_type'] == ft, 'price_pence'].values for ft in fuel_order]
fig_box, ax_box = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
bp = ax_box.boxplot(box_data, labels=fuel_order, patch_artist=True, showfliers=True,
                    flierprops=dict(marker='o', markersize=2, alpha=0.3),
                    whiskerprops=dict(linewidth=1.2),
                    medianprops=dict(linewidth=2, color='#1F2937'),
                    capprops=dict(linewidth=1.2))
for patch, ft in zip(bp['boxes'], fuel_order):
    patch.set_facecolor(PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL))
    patch.set_alpha(0.7)
ax_box.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)')
ax_box.set_xlabel('Fuel Type')
ax_box.set_title('Price Distribution by Fuel Type (all data including outliers)')
fig_box.tight_layout()
chart_box_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_box)

# Chart 2b: Box plot with outliers removed for better visibility
fig_box2, ax_box2 = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
box_data_clipped = []
for ft in fuel_order:
    s = df.loc[df['fuel_type'] == ft, 'price_pence']
    q1, q3 = s.quantile(0.25), s.quantile(0.75)
    iqr = q3 - q1
    lo = q1 - 3 * iqr
    hi = q3 + 3 * iqr
    box_data_clipped.append(s[(s >= lo) & (s <= hi)].values)
bp2 = ax_box2.boxplot(box_data_clipped, labels=fuel_order, patch_artist=True, showfliers=True,
                      flierprops=dict(marker='o', markersize=2, alpha=0.3),
                      whiskerprops=dict(linewidth=1.2),
                      medianprops=dict(linewidth=2, color='#1F2937'),
                      capprops=dict(linewidth=1.2))
for patch, ft in zip(bp2['boxes'], fuel_order):
    patch.set_facecolor(PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL))
    patch.set_alpha(0.7)
ax_box2.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)')
ax_box2.set_xlabel('Fuel Type')
ax_box2.set_title('Price Distribution by Fuel Type (extreme outliers excluded for clarity)')
fig_box2.tight_layout()
chart_box2_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_box2)

# Chart 2c: Violin plot (clip extreme outliers for visibility)
fig_violin, ax_violin = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
violin_data = []
for ft in fuel_order:
    s = df.loc[df['fuel_type'] == ft, 'price_pence']
    q1, q3 = s.quantile(0.25), s.quantile(0.75)
    iqr = q3 - q1
    lo = q1 - 3 * iqr
    hi = q3 + 3 * iqr
    violin_data.append(s[(s >= lo) & (s <= hi)].values)
parts = ax_violin.violinplot(violin_data, positions=range(1, len(fuel_order)+1),
                              showmeans=True, showmedians=True, showextrema=False)
for i, pc in enumerate(parts['bodies']):
    pc.set_facecolor(PALETTE.get(fuel_order[i], NEUTRAL))
    pc.set_alpha(0.6)
parts['cmeans'].set_color('#1F2937')
parts['cmeans'].set_linewidth(1.5)
parts['cmedians'].set_color('#DC2626')
parts['cmedians'].set_linewidth(1.5)
ax_violin.set_xticks(range(1, len(fuel_order)+1))
ax_violin.set_xticklabels(fuel_order)
ax_violin.set_ylabel('Price (pence per litre)')
ax_violin.set_xlabel('Fuel Type')
ax_violin.set_title('Price Density by Fuel Type (Violin Plot)')
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
legend_elements = [Line2D([0], [0], color='#1F2937', linewidth=1.5, label='Mean'),
                   Line2D([0], [0], color='#DC2626', linewidth=1.5, label='Median')]
ax_violin.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='upper right', fontsize=9)
fig_violin.tight_layout()
chart_violin_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_violin)

# Chart 2d: Histograms for major fuel types
major_fuels = [ft for ft in fuel_order if price_stats.loc[ft, 'count'] > 500]
fig_hist, axes_hist = plt.subplots(1, len(major_fuels), figsize=(4*len(major_fuels), 4.5), sharey=True)
if len(major_fuels) == 1:
    axes_hist = [axes_hist]
for ax, ft in zip(axes_hist, major_fuels):
    s = df.loc[df['fuel_type'] == ft, 'price_pence']
    q1, q3 = s.quantile(0.25), s.quantile(0.75)
    iqr = q3 - q1
    lo = q1 - 3 * iqr
    hi = q3 + 3 * iqr
    clipped = s[(s >= lo) & (s <= hi)]
    ax.hist(clipped, bins=40, color=PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL), alpha=0.75, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5)
    ax.set_title(ft, fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    ax.set_xlabel('Price (ppl)')
    if ax == axes_hist[0]:
        ax.set_ylabel('Frequency')
fig_hist.suptitle('Price Histograms by Fuel Type (extreme outliers excluded)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
fig_hist.tight_layout()
chart_hist_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_hist)

# ── Section 3: Price Spread ───────────────────────────────────────────────
print("Analysing price spread...")
spread_data = price_stats[['spread', 'iqr', 'q25', 'q75']].copy()

# Chart 3a: Spread bar chart
fig_spread, ax_spread = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
x_pos = range(len(fuel_order))
ax_spread.bar(x_pos, spread_data.loc[fuel_order, 'spread'],
              color=[PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL) for ft in fuel_order],
              alpha=0.8, edgecolor='white', label='Max - Min Spread')
ax_spread.bar(x_pos, spread_data.loc[fuel_order, 'iqr'],
              color=[PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL) for ft in fuel_order],
              alpha=0.45, edgecolor='white', label='IQR')
ax_spread.set_xticks(x_pos)
ax_spread.set_xticklabels(fuel_order)
ax_spread.set_ylabel('Price Spread (ppl)')
ax_spread.set_title('Price Spread vs Interquartile Range by Fuel Type')
ax_spread.legend()
for i, ft in enumerate(fuel_order):
    ax_spread.text(i, spread_data.loc[ft, 'spread'] + 0.5,
                   f"{spread_data.loc[ft, 'spread']:.1f}",
                   ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold')
fig_spread.tight_layout()
chart_spread_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_spread)

# Chart 3b: IQR lollipop
fig_iqr, ax_iqr = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
for i, ft in enumerate(reversed(fuel_order)):
    q25 = spread_data.loc[ft, 'q25']
    q75 = spread_data.loc[ft, 'q75']
    med = price_stats.loc[ft, 'median']
    clr = PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL)
    ax_iqr.hlines(y=i, xmin=q25, xmax=q75, color=clr, linewidth=6, alpha=0.7)
    ax_iqr.plot(med, i, 'o', color=clr, markersize=10, zorder=5)
    ax_iqr.text(q75 + 0.5, i, f'{q25:.1f}–{q75:.1f}', va='center', fontsize=9)
ax_iqr.set_yticks(range(len(fuel_order)))
ax_iqr.set_yticklabels(list(reversed(fuel_order)))
ax_iqr.set_xlabel('Price (pence per litre)')
ax_iqr.set_title('Interquartile Range by Fuel Type (25th–75th Percentile)')
fig_iqr.tight_layout()
chart_iqr_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_iqr)

# ── Section 4: Update Freshness ───────────────────────────────────────────
print("Analysing update freshness...")
df['update_lag_hours'] = (df['recorded_at'] - df['source_updated_at']).dt.total_seconds() / 3600

lag_stats = df.groupby('fuel_type')['update_lag_hours'].agg(
    count='count',
    mean='mean',
    median='median',
    std='std',
    min='min',
    max='max',
    q25=lambda x: x.quantile(0.25),
    q75=lambda x: x.quantile(0.75),
).sort_values('count', ascending=False)

overall_median_lag = df['update_lag_hours'].median()
overall_mean_lag = df['update_lag_hours'].mean()
pct_under_1h = (df['update_lag_hours'] < 1).mean() * 100
pct_under_24h = (df['update_lag_hours'] < 24).mean() * 100
pct_over_168h = (df['update_lag_hours'] > 168).mean() * 100
pct_negative = (df['update_lag_hours'] < 0).mean() * 100

station_lag = df.groupby('node_id')['update_lag_hours'].median()
stations_stale = int((station_lag > 168).sum())
pct_stations_stale = stations_stale / len(station_lag) * 100
total_stations = len(station_lag)

# Chart 4a: Lag distribution
fig_lag, ax_lag = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
lag_capped = df['update_lag_hours'].clip(upper=500)
for ft in fuel_order:
    subset = lag_capped[df['fuel_type'] == ft]
    ax_lag.hist(subset, bins=60, alpha=0.5, color=PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL), label=ft, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.3)
ax_lag.set_xlabel('Update Lag (hours, capped at 500)')
ax_lag.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax_lag.set_title('Distribution of Update Lag by Fuel Type')
ax_lag.legend(fontsize=9)
fig_lag.tight_layout()
chart_lag_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_lag)

# Chart 4b: Lag box plot
fig_lag_box, ax_lag_box = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
lag_box_data = [df.loc[df['fuel_type'] == ft, 'update_lag_hours'].clip(upper=500).values for ft in fuel_order]
bp_lag = ax_lag_box.boxplot(lag_box_data, labels=fuel_order, patch_artist=True, showfliers=False,
                             whiskerprops=dict(linewidth=1.2),
                             medianprops=dict(linewidth=2, color='#1F2937'),
                             capprops=dict(linewidth=1.2))
for patch, ft in zip(bp_lag['boxes'], fuel_order):
    patch.set_facecolor(PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL))
    patch.set_alpha(0.7)
ax_lag_box.set_ylabel('Update Lag (hours, capped at 500)')
ax_lag_box.set_xlabel('Fuel Type')
ax_lag_box.set_title('Update Lag Distribution by Fuel Type (outliers hidden)')
fig_lag_box.tight_layout()
chart_lag_box_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_lag_box)

# Chart 4c: Lag over time
df['recorded_date'] = df['recorded_at'].dt.date
lag_by_date = df.groupby('recorded_date')['update_lag_hours'].median()
fig_lag_time, ax_lag_time = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.5))
ax_lag_time.plot(lag_by_date.index, lag_by_date.values, color='#2563EB', linewidth=1.5, marker='o', markersize=3)
ax_lag_time.set_xlabel('Date')
ax_lag_time.set_ylabel('Median Update Lag (hours)')
ax_lag_time.set_title('Median Update Lag Over Time')
ax_lag_time.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=30)
fig_lag_time.tight_layout()
chart_lag_time_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_lag_time)

# ── Section 5: Station Coverage ───────────────────────────────────────────
print("Analysing station coverage...")
station_fuel_count = df.groupby('node_id')['fuel_type'].nunique()
ft_per_station = station_fuel_count.value_counts().sort_index()
fuel_station_coverage = df.groupby('fuel_type')['node_id'].nunique().sort_values(ascending=False)
fuel_station_pct = (fuel_station_coverage / total_stations * 100)

# Chart 5a: Fuel types per station
fig_ft_count, ax_ft_count = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))
ax_ft_count.bar(ft_per_station.index, ft_per_station.values, color='#2563EB', alpha=0.8, edgecolor='white')
ax_ft_count.set_xlabel('Number of Fuel Types Reported')
ax_ft_count.set_ylabel('Number of Stations')
ax_ft_count.set_title('Distribution of Fuel Types per Station')
for k, v in ft_per_station.items():
    ax_ft_count.text(k, v + total_stations * 0.005, f'{v:,}', ha='center', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold')
fig_ft_count.tight_layout()
chart_ft_count_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_ft_count)

# Chart 5b: Station coverage by fuel type
fig_coverage, ax_coverage = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
ft_sorted = fuel_station_coverage.index.tolist()
y_pos = range(len(ft_sorted))
ax_coverage.barh(y_pos, fuel_station_coverage.values,
                 color=[PALETTE.get(ft, NEUTRAL) for ft in ft_sorted], alpha=0.8, edgecolor='white')
ax_coverage.set_yticks(y_pos)
ax_coverage.set_yticklabels(ft_sorted)
ax_coverage.set_xlabel('Number of Stations Reporting')
ax_coverage.set_title('Station Coverage by Fuel Type')
for i, (ft, count) in enumerate(zip(ft_sorted, fuel_station_coverage.values)):
    ax_coverage.text(count + total_stations * 0.005, i,
                     f'{count:,} ({fuel_station_pct[ft]:.1f}%)',
                     va='center', fontsize=9)
fig_coverage.tight_layout()
chart_coverage_b64 = fig_to_b64(fig_coverage)

# ── Section 6: Key Findings ───────────────────────────────────────────────
findings = []

    'num': 1,
    'title': f'{most_expensive} is the most expensive fuel type; {least_expensive} the cheapest',
    'detail': (
        f"The average price of {most_expensive} is {price_stats.loc[most_expensive, 'mean']:.1f} ppl, "
        f"compared to {least_expensive} at {price_stats.loc[least_expensive, 'mean']:.1f} ppl "
        f"— a difference of {price_stats.loc[most_expensive, 'mean'] - price_stats.loc[least_expensive, 'mean']:.1f} ppl. "
        f"Premium diesel commands a substantial premium over standard fuels, which is expected but the magnitude warrants continued monitoring."
    ),
    'implication': 'Policy focus should be on ensuring premium fuel pricing is transparent and that consumers are not inadvertently purchasing premium grades at inflated margins.'
})

max_spread_ft = price_stats['spread'].idxmax()
e10_iqr = price_stats.loc['E10', 'iqr'] if 'E10' in price_stats.index else 0

findings.append({
    'num': 2,
    'title': f'Significant price disparities exist within fuel types, especially {max_spread_ft}',
    'detail': (
        f"The raw price spread (max - min) for {max_spread_ft} is {price_stats.loc[max_spread_ft, 'spread']:.1f} ppl, "
        f"though this is inflated by erroneous outlier prices (e.g., prices below 100p or above 250p). "
        f"More meaningfully, the IQR indicates consumers in the middle 50% of stations "
        f"face a price band of {e10_iqr:.1f} ppl (E10) to {b7_iqr:.1f} ppl (B7_STANDARD). "

        f"£{e10_iqr*50/100:.2f} and £{b7_iqr*50/100:.2f} more depending on which station they visit."
    ),
    'implication': 'These disparities suggest either local market power or information asymmetry. Strengthening price transparency tools and promoting real-time comparison could improve consumer outcomes.'
})

findings.append({
    'num': 3,
    'title': 'Most price updates are timely, but a notable tail of stale data exists',
    'detail': (
        f"The median update lag is {overall_median_lag:.1f} hours. "
        f"{pct_under_1h:.1f} pct of records have a lag under 1 hour, and {pct_under_24h:.1f} pct under 24 hours. "

least_covered = fuel_station_coverage.idxmin()

  body {{ font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', sans-serif; color: var(--text); background: var(--bg); line-height: 1.6; }}
  .container {{ max-width: 1060px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 0 24px; }}
  .report-header {{ background: var(--primary); color: #fff; padding: 48px 0 36px; margin-bottom: 40px; }}
  .report-header h1 {{ font-size: 1.75rem; font-weight: 700; margin-bottom: 8px; }}
  .report-header .subtitle {{ font-size: 1rem; opacity: 0.85; font-weight: 400; }}
  .report-header .meta {{ margin-top: 16px; font-size: 0.85rem; opacity: 0.7; }}
  .report-header .meta span {{ margin-right: 24px; }}
  section {{ margin-bottom: 56px; }}
  section h2 {{ font-size: 1.35rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--primary); border-bottom: 3px solid var(--accent); padding-bottom: 8px; margin-bottom: 20px; }}
  section h3 {{ font-size: 1.1rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--primary); margin: 20px 0 10px; }}
  p {{ margin-bottom: 12px; color: var(--text); }}
  .kpi-grid {{ display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(180px, 1fr)); gap: 16px; margin-bottom: 28px; }}
  .kpi-card {{ background: var(--bg-alt); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 8px; padding: 16px 18px; text-align: center; }}
  .kpi-card .kpi-value {{ font-size: 1.6rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--accent); }}
  .kpi-card .kpi-label {{ font-size: 0.78rem; color: var(--text-muted); margin-top: 4px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.5px; }}
  table {{ width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; margin: 16px 0 24px; font-size: 0.9rem; }}
  table thead {{ background: var(--primary); color: #fff; }}
  table th {{ padding: 10px 12px; text-align: left; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.82rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.4px; }}
  table td {{ padding: 9px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); }}
  table tbody tr:hover {{ background: var(--accent-light); }}
  table tbody tr:nth-child(even) {{ background: var(--bg-alt); }}
  table tbody tr:nth-child(even):hover {{ background: var(--accent-light); }}
  .chart-container {{ margin: 24px 0; text-align: center; }}
  .chart-container img {{ max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: 0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.08); }}
  .finding {{ background: var(--bg-alt); border-left: 4px solid var(--accent); border-radius: 0 6px 6px 0; padding: 18px 20px; margin-bottom: 18px; }}
  .finding .finding-num {{ font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--accent); text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 1px; margin-bottom: 4px; }}
  .finding .finding-title {{ font-size: 1.05rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--primary); margin-bottom: 6px; }}
  .finding .finding-detail {{ font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--text); margin-bottom: 8px; }}
  .finding .finding-implication {{ font-size: 0.88rem; color: var(--text-muted); border-top: 1px solid var(--border); padding-top: 8px; }}
  .finding .finding-implication strong {{ color: var(--accent); }}
  .report-footer {{ border-top: 2px solid var(--border); padding: 20px 0; margin-top: 40px; font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--text-muted); text-align: center; }}
  .callout {{ background: #FEF3C7; border-left: 4px solid var(--warning); padding: 14px 18px; border-radius: 0 6px 6px 0; margin: 16px 0; font-size: 0.9rem; }}
  .callout strong {{ color: #92400E; }}
</style>
